title: Introduction to career selection
competency: Explain what career selection is and why it matters.

keywords.def: Choosing an occupation or profession you will follow for a significant period of life, which gives chances for progress and prosperity.
All the roles of one's working life: education, training, and paid and unpaid work.

en.text: Career selection is choosing an occupation you will follow for a significant part of your life, one that gives chances for progress and prosperity. A career includes all your life roles: education, training, and paid and unpaid work. Today it is more complex because mass media shapes many personal choices. After Grade 8, paths include more school, college, trade school, or direct work.

screens.title: Many roads
screens.ask: After Grade 8, which of these is a possible path?
opts: All of them: more school, trade school, college later, or work
screens.after: Figure 1.1 shows the road splitting into college, 2-year college, direct to work, military and trade school.

screens.title: Career selection
paras: Career selection is a process of choosing an occupation or profession that is adopted for a significant period of someone's life and provides opportunities for progress and prosperity.
A career includes all the roles of one's life: education, training, and paid and unpaid work.
In the 21st century, career selection is more complex because mass media plays a big role in shaping personal choices.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Choosing an occupation or profession you will follow for a significant period of life, which gives chances for progress and prosperity.

screens.text: Why has career selection become more complex in the 21st century?
opts: Mass media strongly shapes personal choices
screens.ans: Mass media strongly shapes personal choices

screens.text: Abebe wants to be a footballer only because he saw famous players on TV. What should he do first?
opts: Research careers in his area and check his own skills and resources
screens.ans: Research careers in his area and check his own skills and resources
screens.why: Media can push choices; the four steps (research, evaluation, discussion, decision) help a person choose with real information.
